units.title: Complementary incenter and excenter heights across a reflected side
units.statement: In a right triangle ABC with B=(0,0), A=(a,0), C=(0,c), D=(d,0), and E=(-d,0), let I be the incenter of ACE and J the A-excenter of ACD. Put r=AC and s=CD. Then the heights above AB are c(a+d)/(r+s+a+d) and c(r+s)/(r+s+a+d), respectively. Their sum is BC=c, so the midpoint of IJ lies on the perpendicular bisector of BC.
steps: Express the incenter and opposite-A excenter by side-length weights
Add the two heights and locate the midpoint of IJ
